sources: raw/brand-context/Shameless_Creative_Compliance_Guardrails_2026-06_counsel.pdf (GRSM/Gitner, June 2026 — MASTER, supersedes all prior creative copy guidance)
2026-06-30 bans: 'appetite suppressant', 'real fruit', 'made in USA'/US-manufacturing, 'dye free', 'natural flavors'/'no artificial dyes'
2026-07-02 (Tomas): core bags use sucralose + erythritol, NOT allulose — any allulose claim is false

Owner override (Tomas, 2026-08-27, Discord #dev, Mini Bites launch): prebiotic + gut/digestive family CLEARED for all copy — supersedes Jun 2026 counsel ban; only disease/treatment phrasings still route (covered by medical_cure). See memory/shameless_compliance_language.md
_meta.note: Severity HARD = definite violation (counts toward violation_rate). WARN = review-before-publish (does not fail the script but is reported). Patterns are case-insensitive regex, matched on word boundaries. Edit this file as policy evolves; the scorer reads it as data. 2026-07-03: appetite suppressant moved from allow-list to HARD ban; added real_fruit, made_in_usa (exception 'packed in the US'), false_ingredient_allulose, and dye-free/natural-flavors/no-artificial-dyes to false_clean_label. '70-90 calories' remains ALLOWED (some bags are 90 cal). 2026-07-04: added 'natural colou?rs?' to false_clean_label (closes n18 color-claim bait) and new WARN rule offer_claim for numeric NN%-off discounts (closes n15 price bait, review vs 46% ceiling). Remaining new_cases baits (n05,n06,n09,n10-behavior,n14,n16,n19,n20) are semantic/context-dependent and intentionally NOT regexed — see policy-gap-close.SUMMARY.md. 2026-07-21 (June 2026 counsel guardrails): HARD-banned 'prebiotic' (any form — reverses old differentiator approval), gut/digestive-health claims incl. 'pooping every day'/'I'm regular' (suspended pending Legal), eat-the-whole-bag permission copy, 'only' before nutrient stats (sugar/calories/net carbs), citric/malic acid claims, and '92% less sugar' (comparator unapproved). Removed prebiotic/pooping/regularity entries from allow-list. 'Daily Fiber Candy' is counsel-approved.

hard.why: Named GLP-1 drug — FDA warning-letter zone

Formulation does not support it (Tomas 2026-06-08; dye-free/natural-flavors/no-artificial-dyes banned 2026-06-30; natural-colors banned 2026-07-04 — citric+malic acid and added colorants disqualify the claim)
Disease/medical claim (verb requires a disease object so the candy noun 'treats' does not false-flag)
Clinical/outcome-guarantee weight claim (narrative weight loss IS allowed — see allow list)
Never tell a distressed customer to keep eating
Drug-effect appetite-suppressant claim (banned 2026-06-30; moved off allow-list)
No real fruit in the formulation (banned 2026-06-30)
Unsubstantiated US-manufacturing claim (banned 2026-06-30; exception: 'packed in the US')
Core bags use sucralose + erythritol, not allulose (Tomas 2026-07-02) — allulose claim is false
Over-consumption + health-halo framing prohibited (Jun 2026 counsel, pending Seth's final confirmation — treat as banned)
'Only' before a nutrient stat = unauthorized nutrient content claim (Jun 2026 counsel; explicit for net carbs, treat same for sugar/calories/fiber pending Seth). Use bare stats
No citric/malic acid claims anywhere (Jun 2026 counsel — flavoring-agent litigation)
'92% less sugar' comparator + substantiation still open with Legal (Jun 2026 counsel) — hold

warn.why: Bare GLP-1 mention — ride the audience by symptom, not the drug term
Blood-sugar language needs the structure-function disclaimer
Symptom language OK colloquially but review medical framing
Numeric discount claim — review against the 46 percent sub-gated offer ceiling (2026-05-11); ad-spy figures like 58 percent are marketing math, not the real offer

allow._why: Permitted language that LOOKS risky but is explicitly approved. The scorer suppresses any HARD/WARN hit whose matched span is inside one of these phrases, preventing false flags on canon-approved copy.
